wallSecondsNote: wall time covers ranex run plus gate evaluate inside the emulated guest; journal verify returned PASS chain=verified external-anchor=UNVERIFIED (exit 0) for all six
eligibleForComparisonAReason: Ranex at 131f280a issued real verdicts on all six patches through its own documented external-repository interface (keygen, committed keyring and gate catalog written before each patch, run, gate evaluate with an authenticated approver, journal verify) on an x86-64 Linux executor with unprivileged user namespaces. Conditions to publish with the rows: (1) the executor is QEMU TCG full-system emulation of x86-64 on Apple Silicon, with Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor userns restriction lifted by sysctl; (2) for this Node fixture the only bindable claim is exit-code-only, since Ranex's JUnit path accepts only pytest and Vitest spellings, so these rows belong in the exit-code-only split, not with JUnit-bound runners; (3) governance was written by the operator (this run), not by Ranex.
remainingLimits: Both test-weakening patches were accepted (PASS): an exit-code-only claim cannot see test bodies, and even Ranex's JUnit manifest freezes test IDs, not bodies (its own documentation says so).
No suite manifest could be frozen for node --test; a Vitest or pytest variant of the fixture would be needed to exercise Ranex's frozen test-ID checks.
The default Ubuntu 24.04 image does not qualify: AppArmor's kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 makes bwrap fail, and ranex run then refuses with exit 2. The sysctl change was required.

The task dispatch/judge/merge flow was not exercised: ranex task judge takes --emitted-worktree/--emitted-commit from a prior task dispatch against the kernel-owned repository and has no --external-repository option; the judging path used is the documented external-repository core loop (run, gate evaluate, journal verify).
run --confinement strict-local (Landlock, seccomp, cgroups, qualified launcher) was not attempted; runs used the default kill-safe bubblewrap execution.
journal verify reports external-anchor=UNVERIFIED; no Rekor witness was used (it would send data to a hosted service, which was not authorized).
Emulation speed: each judgement took about 6 s in the guest; native x86-64 timing will differ.
Setup tools beyond qemu: Homebrew lima-additional-guestagents 2.2.0 (needed for any x86_64 Lima guest), NodeSource apt repository for Node 24, uv 0.8.22 from astral.sh.
